LHX.sentence: L3Harris has fallen more than 30% from its high — unusually steep for a steady defense company — even though military spending keeps rolling along, so the business is fine and the stock is just unusually beaten down.

ASML.sentence: ASML drifted up a little this week, and nothing's changed about the core story — they're still the only company on earth making the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is quiet — the world's biggest supplier of oxygen, nitrogen and other industrial gases just keeps delivering under long contracts, though it's priced a touch closer to its rivals than usual.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is dead calm this week, though it has quietly outrun its peers over the past month as the Azure cloud and AI story keeps grinding forward without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher, the lab-equipment supplier to the whole biotech and research world, is sitting right near its highs after a solid week — nothing dramatic going on.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge, the Canadian pipeline operator that collects tolls on the oil and gas it moves, is flat and pays a healthy dividend, though it's fairly priced rather than a screaming bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow slipped a little and is down meaningfully from its high, but big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI workflow tools, and it's still outrunning its software rivals.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore barely moved even though copper prices have been surging lately — a bit of a disconnect, since this miner and trader usually benefits when copper runs.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is down slightly, but the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still climbing — each quarry effectively has its own local market no one else can serve — and the dip looks like the construction cycle, not a weakening business.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA dipped a bit, mostly because a weaker Mexican peso shrinks the value of its earnings once they're converted back to dollars.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras was quiet, but with oil prices running high this is a strong stretch for the Brazilian oil giant's earnings and its famously big dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant, jumped nearly 4% and is priced so cheaply the market is practically valuing its ships below what it'd cost to replace them.

MA.sentence: Mastercard eased off a little and is actually priced slightly below Visa right now, which is rare since it usually trades at a premium — people keep tapping their cards constantly, so this is more about mood than the business.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot maker had a soft day but has been a strong performer this past month — hospitals keep doing more robot-assisted operations, and each one sells more of the instruments and supplies that drive its profits.
